# Step 4: what reaches the tubes and the speaker (generated by r4_residue.py)

1. Supply-to-speaker transfer of the power stage at the switching frequencies: the power amp's
   stage.py (read only, 99cff1f: 4 tubes, 1650TA, 220 nF / 91k, 1k screen resistors, 8 ohm), bias
   solved for 70 % idle, PI outputs idle (10 kohm to ground), an AC source on V_ANODE or on V_SCREEN
   directly at the centre tap / screen node (the residue of r2 is already the voltage after the power
   amp's 100 nF); matched tubes and +-5 % idle mismatch between the sides; KT88 and EL34.
   Limit: the 1650TA model has leakage and DCR but no winding capacitance (its real self-resonances
   at 50-200 kHz are not modelled).
2. Residue at the speaker for the r2 operating points (recommended chain, ESR 0.3 ohm), anode and
   screen added in phase (worst), against today's hard-switched design and the proposed target.
3. Beat and intermodulation products: a transient of the same stage with V_ANODE and V_SCREEN each
   carrying a 1 V sine at different frequencies (two free-running bridges: 47.3 / 41 kHz) and a 1 kHz
   drive to about 10 W; the products f_a - f_s and f_sw +- f_audio at the speaker scale with the
   product of the two residues (bilinear), so they are reported scaled to the real residue amplitudes.
4. Aliasing in the loop: the first capacitor's current carries the TCM triangle (+-1 A); sampled
   asynchronously at 31.25 kSPS it folds into the audio band and enters v_sw through Kc. Output
   disturbance with the r3 loop, against synchronous sampling (mid-conduction CNV: no alias).
5. Conducted noise: the raw-rail figures of r2 (section 5) and the switch-node edges (r1) as common-
   mode current through the IGBT tabs' capacitance to the heatsinks / chassis.

## 1. Supply-to-speaker transfer (V at the 8 ohm load per V at the supply node)

| Tubes | mismatch | supply | 20 kHz | 40 kHz | 60 kHz | 100 kHz | 150 kHz | 300 kHz |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| KT88 | 0 % | anode | 1.8e-18 | 8.4e-18 | 4.6e-18 | 2.5e-18 | 2.8e-20 | 1.3e-19 |
| KT88 | 0 % | screen | 6.5e-17 | 1.1e-16 | 1.6e-17 | 1.4e-17 | 5.6e-20 | 5.1e-18 |
| KT88 | 5 % | anode | 3.8e-04 | 4.2e-04 | 3.6e-04 | 1.3e-04 | 3.5e-05 | 4.3e-06 |
| KT88 | 5 % | screen | 4.2e-03 | 4.0e-03 | 2.9e-03 | 7.5e-04 | 1.3e-04 | 1.5e-06 |
| EL34 | 0 % | anode | 1.8e-18 | 2.4e-18 | 1.6e-17 | 3.8e-18 | 8.8e-19 | 8.7e-19 |
| EL34 | 0 % | screen | 1.7e-17 | 9.0e-17 | 1.2e-16 | 3.9e-17 | 6.8e-18 | 1.7e-18 |
| EL34 | 5 % | anode | 3.1e-04 | 6.3e-04 | 1.2e-03 | 9.9e-04 | 2.0e-04 | 1.7e-05 |
| EL34 | 5 % | screen | 4.6e-03 | 6.9e-03 | 1.0e-02 | 5.8e-03 | 9.2e-04 | 7.0e-05 |

Reading: the anode residue is common mode in the push-pull primary and reaches the secondary only through the mismatch and the tubes' plate resistance (tens of kilohms); the screen residue modulates both sides' plate currents through the screen transconductance and leaks through the same mismatch; above about 20 kHz the transformer's leakage inductance (64 mH) rolls everything off further.

## 2. Residue at the speaker (uV rms, +-5 % mismatch; anode and screen added in phase)

| Point (anode / screen) | f_sw common (kHz) | residue at the power amp: anode / screen (mV p-p) | speaker KT88 / EL34, recommended (uV rms) | speaker KT88 / EL34, today's hard-switched 50 kHz (uV rms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 400 V 0.7 A / 390 V 0.18 A | 40 | 16.3 / 11.4 | 18.6 / 31.8 | 31.6 / 80.1 |
| 400 V 0.3 A / 390 V 0.12 A | 78 | 3.2 / 2.0 | 1.5 / 7.3 | 42.3 / 107.1 |
| 200 V 0.35 A / 195 V 0.1 A | 150 | 1.5 / 0.7 | 0.0 / 0.3 | 147.4 / 369.5 |
| 150 V 0.2 A / 146 V 0.08 A | 150 | 1.3 / 0.6 | 0.0 / 0.3 | 131.2 / 329.5 |
| 20 V 0.5 A / 20 V 0.0 A | 49 | 8.6 / 4.0 | 6.4 / 15.6 | 21.3 / 53.9 |

Worst with the recommended chain: 32 uV rms, all of it at 40-150 kHz (today's design: up to about 150-300 uV at mid voltage). Proposed target: switching residue at the speaker <= 50 uV rms (-86 dBV; a valve power stage's own hum and noise at the speaker is typically 0.1-1 mV, and the residue is ultrasonic), at the power amp's supply inputs <= 20 mV p-p (nominal ESR), and no product of the switching inside 20 Hz-20 kHz above 1 uV (-120 dBV).

## 3. Beat and intermodulation products (KT88, +-5 % mismatch, transient)

1 V sines on V_ANODE (47.3 kHz) and V_SCREEN (41 kHz), 1 kHz drive (about 10 W) or none. Products at the speaker (V peak, Hann window over 30 ms):

| Case | 6.3 kHz (f_a - f_s) | 47.3 kHz | 41 kHz | 46.3 / 48.3 kHz (f_a -+ 1 kHz) | 1 kHz fundamental |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| anode 1 V, screen 1 V, drive on | 8.9e-06 | 1.2e-04 | 7.3e-04 | 7.8e-03 / 7.9e-03 | 41.62 |
| anode 1 V, screen 0 V, drive on | 1.3e-05 | 1.2e-04 | 2.2e-04 | 7.8e-03 / 7.9e-03 | 41.62 |
| anode 0 V, screen 1 V, drive on | 6.3e-07 | 4.9e-08 | 7.3e-04 | 2.3e-09 / 5.7e-09 | 41.62 |
| anode 1 V, screen 1 V, drive off | 4.0e-06 | 4.1e-04 | 4.0e-03 | 9.2e-11 / 4.1e-11 | 0.00 |

The difference product with both supplies carrying 1 V is 8.9e-06 V (the single-supply runs show the numerical floor at that bin, 1.3e-05 V). Scaled to the real residues (about 14 mV and 4 mV peak at the low end of the band: x 5.6e-05) it is 5.0e-10 V: far below 1 uV. The audio sidebands f_sw +- f_audio stay above 20 kHz. So with residues this small the bridges need not be synchronised for the speaker's sake; they should be for the loop's sampling (section 4) and the raw rail (r2 section 5: interleaving at a common frequency halves the input ripple current and cuts the PSU-cable ripple 4x).

## 4. Aliasing of the TCM ripple in the loop (V_ANODE, today's schedule, r3 gains)

| f_sw (kHz) | I_C ripple fundamental after the 2 us filter (A peak) | alias frequency at 31.25 kSPS (Hz) | output disturbance, asynchronous sampling (mV peak) | synchronous mid-conduction sampling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 40.0 | 0.65 | 8750 | 4 (with the synchronous gains: 20) | none: the sample lands where the triangle crosses its average (offset < 50 mA for 50 ns of timing error) |
| 47.0 | 0.53 | 15500 | 1 (with the synchronous gains: 3) | none: the sample lands where the triangle crosses its average (offset < 50 mA for 50 ns of timing error) |
| 62.6 | 0.54 | 100 | 147 (with the synchronous gains: 312) | none: the sample lands where the triangle crosses its average (offset < 50 mA for 50 ns of timing error) |
| 94.0 | 0.30 | 250 | 134 (with the synchronous gains: 313) | none: the sample lands where the triangle crosses its average (offset < 50 mA for 50 ns of timing error) |
| 125.3 | 0.84 | 300 | 408 (with the synchronous gains: 952) | none: the sample lands where the triangle crosses its average (offset < 50 mA for 50 ns of timing error) |
| 150.0 | 0.61 | 6250 | 12 (with the synchronous gains: 57) | none: the sample lands where the triangle crosses its average (offset < 50 mA for 50 ns of timing error) |

Asynchronous sampling turns the ripple into an audio-band tone of up to 408 mV at the output whose frequency moves with f_sw (and with the load, in the adaptive law): the TCM bridge needs the ADC's CNV timed by the PWM generator, in the middle of a high-side conduction interval of the bridge being sampled (or an anti-alias filter, which costs the phase the damping needs).

## 5. Conducted noise

| Quantity | Today (hard-switched, 50 kHz) | TCM (recommended) |
|---|---|---|
| Switch-node edge rate | 20-50 V/ns (datasheet t_r 4-6 ns; M15) | 1.2-4 V/ns (r1 switching model) |
| Common-mode current through 20 pF (tab + heatsink to chassis) | 0.4-1.0 A peaks, ~10-20 ns | 25-80 mA, 100-400 ns |
| Edge spectrum corner (1 / (pi t_r)) | 16-30 MHz | 0.8-3 MHz |
| Raw node UIN ripple / PSU cable ripple (r2 sec. 5) | 0.19 V p-p / 0.7 mA rms | 0.27-0.6 V p-p / 0.4-2.1 mA rms interleaved (8 mA in phase) |

The soft edges cut the common-mode noise above a few MHz by about 20-25 dB; the differential ripple drawn from the raw rail rises (larger, slower inductor ripple), and stays small on the PSU cable when the two bridges are interleaved at one frequency.
